### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a542de9c6e71766afaa9a9f74b2314660794972` — the merge of head `4258efac241ae1e557a984b3487e81b026ac7425` into base `b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a542de9c6e71766afaa9a9f74b2314660794972 && git checkout 2a542de9c6e71766afaa9a9f74b2314660794972
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef 4258efac241ae1e557a984b3487e81b026ac7425 && git checkout -B drift-repro b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef && git merge --no-ff 4258efac241ae1e557a984b3487e81b026ac7425

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b83baed2b35fbeebfdaeda07943da1e91d904aef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4258efac241ae1e557a984b3487e81b026ac7425`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs` at the head, to derive the two ledger rows; it exited 3 (prerequisite not met, no `typescript` in this container) and measured nothing, so the rows were derived by reading and by the head's green `Engine test-double contract gate` step
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-datasource-credentials-ref.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.datasource-credentials-ref-own-reference.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/datasource-credentials-ref-own-reference.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts (`authoredLockFamily`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`headAt`, `resolveWriteHead`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-save-request.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`SaveMetaItemRequestSchema`), packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts (#27582), scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`.changeset/27762-datasource-meta-save-credentials-ref.md` is a prose face: the lane seat's ACCEPT)

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rule.** The one #27582 set at the engine and #27761 applied at the datasource admin door's create: a non-system write may only seal a new value or keep its own record's stored reference. The metadata save door seals nothing, so its accept set for `datasource.external.credentialsRef` is exactly one value: the one the save's own stored row holds.
- **Accept set, before → after** (`saveMetaItem`: REST `PUT /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name`, the runtime `/meta` door, in-process saves):
  - Before: a body's `external.credentialsRef` was stored as given, on a create, an edit and a draft.
  - Now, refused `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400: a create naming any reference; an edit naming a reference other than its row's, or one where its row holds none; a draft naming one the row it overlays does not hold. **Correct, and exactly the rule.**
  - Still accepted: the GET → edit → PUT round trip (the read serves the reference, the save echoes it); a first draft echoing the active row's reference; a body naming no reference (stores none, as before — omission is not a carry-forward, which is a defensible reading, stated in the PR); the server-stated rewrite (`source` set). All four pinned.
- **One answer whatever the reference names.** The judge compares the body's value with its own row's value only; nothing is looked up; the message names the key and the datasource, never the value. The unit pin asserts equal refusals for a held and an unheld reference and that no message contains any reference; the dogfood pin asserts the same at the REST door. Holds.
- **Q1 — the `args.source !== undefined` pass-through is not reachable from any caller-facing door.** Read on the head tree: the REST route builds the request field by field (`writeFace: 'meta-envelope'`, `metaSaveRequestOptions` answers only `parentVersion` / `mode` / `surface`); the runtime dispatcher does the same (`meta-dispatch`); `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema` (the SDK/MCP request shape) has no `source` member; the only in-process caller that states one is `migrateStoredMetadata` (`'migrate-stored'`). An in-process trusted caller can state it, which is the same shape as the system principal under #27582. No bypass.
- **Q2 — the judge reads the row the save writes.** Its address (`{ type, name, org: 'env' }`, `state` from `mode`, `packageId: request.packageId ?? null`, `member: itemDiscriminator(type, item)`, draft falling back to the active row at `target.packageId`) is line for line `authoredLockFamily`'s read (`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` 620–627) and the save's own write-head read before `repo.put` (`protocol.ts` 21546–21550; the put uses the same `org: 'env'` ref). `org: 'env'` is the only address this method can write: ADR-0131 D6 refuses an organization-scoped request at the method's first line, and `resolveWriteHead` does not key on `ref.org`. Per-package rows: `headAt` resolves the package-bound or unbound row exactly as `put` upserts it (#22128). Bundle members: datasource is not a bundle type; the same `itemDiscriminator` is used on both sides. Drafts: an existing draft row is compared with itself; a first draft with the active row it overlays. Correct.
- **Q3 — placement.** After the per-type schema parse (so `credentialsRef` is a string; `strictObject` refuses alias spellings rather than renaming them) and after the body rewrites the gate sees (`stripReadDecorations`, the lock family), and before `repo.put`, the registry write-through, the audit row, the projector and the mutation event. No store write sits between the method's entry and the judge (the only earlier write is the lock-denial audit row, on a different refusal's path). Reached on every path that writes a datasource: `meta-envelope`, `meta-dispatch`, `package-duplicate` and `package-unmanaged-import` (both pass no `source`), in-process saves, and the plural spelling (canonicalised before the judge). All pinned on the `saveMetaItem` harness with a byte-identical store and an empty write log after each refusal.
- **The remedy stays open.** The datasource admin door persists through `putDatasourceRecord` → `metadata.register` + a direct `sys_metadata` engine write under the system context, not through `saveMetaItem`; the door that mints a reference is not judged by this rule.
- **Published surface:** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gains one unexported module; no export, type or schema moves. `DatasourceSchema` is untouched.
- **Q5 — the ledger.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` enumerates predicate-bound doubles per file and verb, regenerated by `--write` only. The new pin's stub binds `findOne` to `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` and `update` to `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`; `find` and `insert` are not pinned verbs. Two rows, one per bound verb, none lost: derived. The head's `Engine test-double contract gate` step (job `Lint · ESLint`) is green, which is the gate reading that ledger against the discovered set.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: **`minor`**, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and the changeset, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title and one ADR-0087 marker. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor`; `narrowed` is the right kind (a value the acceptance surface stored is now refused). Consistent.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the changeset carries a remedy for the request (echo the served reference, omit the key, or bind through the admin door), not a prescription for rewriting stored data or consumer code; the gate's category reads exactly that distinction; `Check Changeset` is green at the head. Correct.
- `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is present on the PR body with a reason read against `skills/**` (lane seat's ACCEPT to confirm the sentence).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Restore doors and already-stored rows are not re-judged** (`rollbackMetaItem` / `revertCommit` restore history byte for byte for a type with no credential channel, and datasource has none). Accepted as out of scope for this PR closing #27762: the card names the save door, which this head measures, pins and fixes. The seat filed the follow-up as #27818 (restore doors and already-stored rows), rule-level text only.
- **Package copy and unmanaged import are judged.** A copied datasource body naming a reference lands in the copy's `failed[]`; an imported one is refused and `rollBackUnmanagedImport` unwinds the import. Both are the rule applied to a new row that holds nothing of its own, and the shape is stated in the PR. Reachable only for a package-bound stored datasource row that already holds a reference. Accepted; the seat may note it in ACCEPT.
- **Dogfood battery at 7e9b721e:** 3 reds in `error-sentences-live` (2) and `object-hook-lifecycle-scratch` (1), attributed to #27667. Checked by reading: #27667 is 21c4bdd8, the PR's merge-base and on `main`; both files are unchanged between 7e9b721e and `origin/main` and still assert a pre-#27667 code on the hook-abort answer. The attribution is consistent with the tree; main-side, not this change's. The commit after 7e9b721e touches a unit-test double and the ledger only.
- **Stale citation in prose:** the PR body says the engine-double gates "were fixed in 7256944b", which is no commit of this PR (rewritten into 4258efac). Prose only; lane seat's ACCEPT.
- **Check-runs at this head:** no red; `Test Core` shards, `Build Core` and two `Type Check` jobs were still in progress when read. Landing waits for all green.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside-author note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`protocol-datasource-credentials-ref.ts`:** the right altitude. The judge is handed the repository's `headAt` read alone, so it can read and cannot write; it reads the save's own row the way the lock-family judge already reads it, which is the one address the write resolves to; it asks nothing about the reference itself. It holds against #27582's shape (own row only, one answer, nothing written) and against the cited code.
- **`protocol.ts`:** one import and one call-site block beside the other datasource-family save refusals; nothing moves. Holds against the serial-queue rule for that file.
- **Against the published spec on `main`:** `DatasourceSchema` keeps `external.credentialsRef` authorable — for a code-defined datasource (`defineDatasource`), which the package door refuses at this door anyway, and for read-back — and documents that the door that binds a secret writes the reference. The narrowing makes that invariant real at the one consumer that could store a caller's value. No declared capability is taken from a consumer: the Console's datasource page saves through the admin door, and no SDK method sets the key.
- **Tests:** the unit pin drives the real `saveMetaItem` over a stub held to the engine-double predicates, asserts code and status, a byte-identical store and an empty write log on every refusal, and covers each face and both acceptances; the dogfood pin holds the rule at the booted REST door as a non-system caller. The ablation readings in the PR body are consistent with the pin's shape.
